text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya Power and Lighting Company is stuck with 6.0 million litres of kerosene valued at 700 million shillings it cannot use because the Kenya Petroleum Refineries has refused to handle it.

- The management of Nakumatt Holding Limited -- the firm whose trading licence was revoked for allegedly importing contaminated beef -- claims it is a victim of a 50 million shillings extortion attempt.
- Gangsters shoot dead two policemen escorting money to the Central Bank of Kenya and escape with more than 5.0 million shillings.
- Opposition leader Richard Leakey dismisses opposition politicians Mwai Kibaki, Michael Kijana Wamalwa, Martin Shikuku and James Orengo as "the four musketeers".
- Law Society of Kenya (LSK) chairman Paul Wamae says it is unrealistic to describe LSK as insolvent, but admits that there are some weaknesses in its secretariat.
- The National Irrigation Board impounds more than 500 kilogrammes of sub-standard Pishori rice from supermarkets in Nairobi.
- President Daniel arap Moi reiterates that the government is delinking itself from the coffee and tea industries in line with the liberalisation and privatisation programme.
- A permanent secretary in the office of the president blames mismanagement of public funds on some civil servants.
